candidates.summary: the page cap aborts the crawl where its sibling realm cap truncates and reports, so a wide PR loses the whole preview instead of a bounded one
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request that bumps a widely imported p/ package, or touches a realm whose render page links many :p/<arg> views, crosses -max-pages (400). Run returns `page cap 400 reached`, main.go:134 returns before Write, and every captured page is discarded: the render job goes red, no artifact is uploaded, and the publish workflow posts no comment. One level up, plan.go:256-258 meets the same overflow by truncating the realm list and recording plan.Dropped ("never silently"), so the reviewer still gets a preview plus a line naming what was left out. The deeper form is the same shape here: stop enqueueing at the cap, write what was captured, and carry a Truncated count into the comment the way Dropped already is. What the shallow form costs to maintain is two caps on one pipeline with opposite failure modes, and a README (line 118) that calls the page cap a backstop.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test ./... -run PageCap -v with tests/b2-refactor-pagecap_test.go copied in: a Crawler with MaxPages=3 against an httptest gnoweb whose page links ten :p/<n> views
candidates.evidence: Green on the unmodified head worktree: `cap tripped: page cap 3 reached (queue still had 31) — 3 captured pages discarded by the caller`, with the three `✓ /r/x/y`, `✓ /r/x/y$source`, `✓ /r/x/y$help` captures printed before the abort. main.go:134-138 reads `if err := c.Run(); err != nil { return err }` ahead of `c.Write(cfg.out, assets)`, so the captured pages never reach disk.

candidates.summary: Seeds 31 -> 18 lines: the `if !c.RenderOnly` wrapper at line 99 is dead (the same flag already `continue`d before dirs could be filled) and the seen/add closure repeats the dedupe Run applies with `visited`
candidates.failure_scenario: Not a defect: dirs is only written inside the loop body that line 92's `if c.RenderOnly { continue }` skips, so under RenderOnly sortedKeys(dirs) is empty and the guard at line 99 can never change the result. The eight-line add/seen closure dedupes a slice whose only consumer, Run, already skips a repeat through `visited` and stores seeds in a set. Dropping both leaves `for ... { out = append(out, u); ...; }` plus `return append(out, sortedKeys(dirs)...)`: 31 lines become 18, one nesting level and one closure gone. Run's line 117 `queue := append([]string(nil), seeds...)` is the same shape one function over — Seeds returns a fresh slice on every call, so the defensive copy guards nothing and is a nineteenth line to drop.

candidates.summary: chargeFile 29 -> 18 lines: it re-derives (realm, file) from the URL that inScope at line 177 already derived, with two 8-line helpers shared by both (inScope 38 -> 32, 67 -> 66 total but one derivation instead of two)
candidates.failure_scenario: Not a defect today. The per-file budget is tested in wantFile (reached from inScope, which walks the query and matches base against c.Realms) and charged in chargeFile, which walks the query and matches base against c.Realms again with its own spelling: inScope rejects the page if any file= value fails, chargeFile keeps the last file= it sees, and where base is not a selected realm inScope answers false while chargeFile answers true. Extracting `func (c *Crawler) realmOf(base string) string` and `func fileArg(query string) string` gives both one derivation and collapses chargeFile's realm loop to a straight-line body. The cost of leaving it is that the next change to how gnoweb spells the tab query has to land in two functions that already disagree about a repeated file= and about an unselected realm.

candidates.summary: links 19 -> 12 lines: it hand-rolls the dedupe-and-sort that the package's own sortedKeys (plan.go:317) already provides, and its `p == ""` guard cannot fire behind the `HasPrefix(raw, "/")` filter
candidates.failure_scenario: Not a defect. The body keeps `seen`, a parallel `out`, a `seen[p]` test, an append and a trailing sort.Strings for a result that is exactly sortedKeys(seen); the `p == ""` arm is unreachable because raw is already known to start with "/", so the cut at "#" leaves at least "/". `seen[canonicalURL(p)] = true` then `return sortedKeys(seen)` is the same function in 12 lines. One delta to state: sortedKeys returns an allocated empty slice where the original returned nil for a page with no in-site links, and Run's only use is `for _, link := range links(body)`, which cannot tell them apart.

candidates.summary: Write's `assets == ""` sentinel is a mode flag on a path parameter with one call site; exporting writePages removes the branch and names what the caller wants
candidates.failure_scenario: Not a defect. main.go:275 calls `base.Write(cfg.out, "")` to mean "this is the prefixed before-pass, the assets are already on disk", and Write decodes that sentinel into `return c.writePages(dir)`. The method it wants already exists one line down, unexported. Exporting it and calling `base.WritePages(cfg.out)` drops the branch and its comment, and leaves Write's signature saying only what it does. What the sentinel costs: a future caller that genuinely has no assets directory gets the _chroma/style.css fetch silently skipped as well, and the reason is three words in a trailing comment rather than a method name. Same shape as RenderOnly + Prefix + MaxPages=len(realms), all four set together at the single renderBase call site.
candidates.verify_by: rename writePages to WritePages, replace main.go:275 with base.WritePages(cfg.out), drop crawl.go:304-306; cd misc/gnopreview && go build ./... && go test ./...

dropped.summary: slug's `out != ""` beside `out == s` looked like a redundant clause
dropped.settled_by: Both are load-bearing: for s == "" the two are equal and the clause is what routes the empty input to the digest branch instead of returning an empty path segment that path.Join would swallow. `grep -n 'slug(' crawl.go shots.go` shows only urlToFile (args or query already non-empty) and shots.go:76 (a realm path), so removing it would be safe today and unsafe for the next caller — the guard is at the right depth.
